belief: “I’m damaged and ashamed, as if what was done to me made me worthless.”
belief_plain: I’m damaged and ashamed, as if what was done to me made me worthless
origins: Harm can leave shame that feels like a stain: damaged, ashamed, worthless. That feeling is common, and it is a lie about your worth. What was done to you does not make you less of a person. Shame often shows up because someone treated you as if you did not matter. God’s nearness to the brokenhearted is the opposite of that treatment. You do not have to recount what happened to question this sentence. If you are not safe right now, call 911. You can also call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233. If a child is being hurt, call Childhelp at 1-800-422-4453. A counselor can help you at a pace that is safe. You do not have to do this alone, or all at once. If you are thinking about ending your life, call or text 988 in the United States, or tell someone near you right away.
self: If people knew, they would be disgusted.
I will never be worth kindness.
The shame is proof that I am the problem.
I should hide so I do not contaminate anyone.
replacement: I was hurt, and I am not worthless. What was done to me does not decide what I am worth.
